decisions.summary: First establish whether the supported host integration forms a GPL-covered combined work and which components it encompasses. If so, determine the applicable GPL version from those components' grants. The vendor's GPL-2.0-only QEMU label does not automatically set this package's license; GPL-2.0-or-later FFmpeg cannot upgrade any GPL-2.0-only code found to be in scope.

Preserve Apache-2.0 notices for adapted gfxstream declarations. Apache's interface-linking exclusion and the standalone hook support assessing a gfxstream boundary; private ABI use alone does not establish QEMU coverage. Determine any further compatibility requirements only for components within a justified combined-work scope. This evidence does not resolve the SDK host's legal scope.

Inventory any NVIDIA material incorporated into generated PTX and preserve its applicable terms. If the supported host integration is a GPL-covered combined work, assess libcuda and libnvidia-encode compatibility, permissions and any system-library exception under the applicable GPL version. Separate driver installation and MIT interface headers do not establish such an exception.

Inventory actual Frida bootstrap/loader bytes, their source, build recipes and licenses. Audit embedded helper payloads in the standalone injector separately; do not automatically assign the injector's complete libelf/OpenSSL dependency list to the injected agent.

Resolve the host integration's legal scope without assuming all QEMU or SDK source is required. Document which host/renderer sources, if any, must accompany the two native binaries and why other components are excluded. For any required host sources, establish their match to build 15507667; a current branch or stale FFmpeg URL is not an exact match. Host-binary omission alone does not decide scope.
